blueprint_concepts: Maximum and minimum of general trigonometric expressions under constraints
english: Let $S(4,0)$ and $S'(-4,0)$ be the foci of the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{9}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{7}=1$. For a point $P$ on the hyperbola, let $p_{1}$ and $p_{2}$ denote the perpendicular distances of $S$ and $S'$, respectively, from the tangent to the hyperbola at $P$. As $P$ varies over the hyperbola, the least value of $9p_{1}+p_{2}$ is
hindi: माना अतिपरवलय $\dfrac{x^{2}}{9}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{7}=1$ की नाभियाँ $S(4,0)$ तथा $S'(-4,0)$ हैं। अतिपरवलय पर किसी बिन्दु $P$ के लिए, माना $P$ पर अतिपरवलय की स्पर्श रेखा से $S$ तथा $S'$ की लम्बवत् दूरियाँ क्रमशः $p_{1}$ तथा $p_{2}$ हैं। जब $P$ अतिपरवलय पर गति करता है, तब $9p_{1}+p_{2}$ का न्यूनतम मान है
solution: Product of perpendiculars from the foci on any tangent: $p_{1}p_{2}=b^{2}=7$
Right branch ($\sec\theta\ge1$): $\dfrac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\in(1,7]$, largest at $\theta=0$; so $p_{2}^{2}=7\cdot\dfrac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\in(7,49]$, i.e. $p_{2}\in(\sqrt{7},7]$
$9p_{1}+p_{2}=\dfrac{63}{p_{2}}+p_{2}$; AM-GM equality needs $p_{2}=\sqrt{63}>7$, not attainable, and $\dfrac{63}{t}+t$ decreases for $t<\sqrt{63}$
So on the right branch the least value is at $p_{2}=7$, $p_{1}=1$ (vertex $(3,0)$): $9+7=16$
solution_full: Here $a=3$, $b=\sqrt{7}$, $c=4$, $e=\dfrac{4}{3}$. Take $P(3\sec\theta,\sqrt{7}\tan\theta)$; $\sec\theta>0$ on the right branch and $\sec\theta<0$ on the left branch.

Product: $p_{1}p_{2}=\dfrac{\frac{16}{9}\sec^{2}\theta-1}{N^{2}}=\dfrac{63(16\sec^{2}\theta-9)}{9(7\sec^{2}\theta+9\tan^{2}\theta)}=\dfrac{7(16\sec^{2}\theta-9)}{16\sec^{2}\theta-9}=7$. This is the property that the product of the perpendiculars from the foci on any tangent equals $b^{2}$.

Ratio: $\dfrac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}=\left|\dfrac{4\sec\theta+3}{4\sec\theta-3}\right|$. On the right branch, $\sec\theta\ge1$, so the ratio is greater than $1$ and is largest, equal to $\dfrac{7}{1}=7$, at $\sec\theta=1$; as $\sec\theta\to\infty$ it tends to $1$. Hence $\dfrac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\in(1,7]$.

Now $9p_{1}+p_{2}=\dfrac{63}{p_{2}}+p_{2}=g(p_{2})$. AM-GM gives $g\ge2\sqrt{63}=6\sqrt{7}$ with equality only at $p_{2}=\sqrt{63}\approx7.94$, which is outside $(\sqrt{7},7]$. Since $g'(t)=1-\dfrac{63}{t^{2}}<0$ for $t<\sqrt{63}$, $g$ is decreasing on $(\sqrt{7},7]$ and its least value is $g(7)=9+7=16$, attained at the vertex $(3,0)$, where the tangent $x=3$ gives $p_{1}=1$, $p_{2}=7$.

On the left branch the roles of the foci are exchanged: $p_{1}\in(\sqrt{7},7]$, $p_{2}=\dfrac{7}{p_{1}}$, and $9p_{1}+\dfrac{7}{p_{1}}$ is increasing there (derivative $9-\dfrac{7}{p_{1}^{2}}>0$), so its values exceed $10\sqrt{7}>16$; at the vertex $(-3,0)$ it equals $64$.
Hence the least value is $16$. Option (A) is the unattainable AM-GM bound.
originality_note: New: a weighted sum of the two focal perpendiculars on a tangent is minimised under the constraint p1 p2 = b^2 with the ratio p2/p1 confined to (1, 7], so the AM-GM point is not attainable and the minimum sits at the vertex (way 4). Closest known: product of perpendiculars from the foci on a tangent equals b^2. Different because: the extremum is decided by the trigonometric range of the ratio, not by AM-GM.

concept_use.Miscellaneous properties of Hyperbola: The property p1 p2 = b^2 = 7 for the perpendiculars from the foci on any tangent turns 9 p1 + p2 into a function of one variable.
concept_use.Maximum and minimum of general trigonome: The ratio p2/p1 = (4 sec(theta) + 3)/(4 sec(theta) - 3) is confined to (1, 7] by sec(theta) >= 1, and the minimum is taken under this constraint (the AM-GM point is excluded).

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve, point and symbol is introduced, every condition is stated, there is one reading of each sentence; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no asymptote wording. Checked that P ranges over both branches and the least value 16 is attained (at (3,0)), so 'least value' is correct; the trap value 6 sqrt 7 is not attained. Changed: No change.
key_step: p1 p2 = 7 with p2/p1 in (1, 7], so 63/p2 + p2 is decreasing on the allowed range and the minimum is at the vertex.
justification: Two ideas linked: the focal-perpendicular product property and a constrained extremum where the obvious AM-GM value is a trap. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q13 (L3) on hyperbola properties; the trap and range check keep it at 3 rather than 2.
